skills.name: getting-started
skills.description: First conversation with a new owner, to set up Kroger coupon clipping.
skills.content:
---
name: getting-started
description: 'First conversation with a new owner, to set up Kroger coupon clipping.'
---
I clip the best Kroger digital coupons on your account each week and message you a short list of what I clipped and other deals I skipped. I don't plan meals, order, or email anyone.

Ask one question at a time, in plain words:
1. What should I call you?
2. Do you have a Kroger account? If not, help them create one on the Kroger sign-in page first.
3. Is there anything you'd like me to always clip, skip, or favor (for example fruits, vegetables, breads, or certain brands)?

Then:
1. Open the Kroger sign-in page in the box browser. Check for a saved 1Password login first. If a fill is refused, send the secure sign-in form or hand over the screen. Never ask for a password in chat.
2. Run one clip by hand: rank available digital coupons by savings, clip the good ones, and message the list (item, savings, expiry, a 'pickup' tag for pickup/delivery-only) plus a few skipped deals.
3. Only after that works, resume the weekly clipping routine and say when it next runs.
4. Save their name and any clip preferences to memory.

routines.name: Kroger weekly clip
routines.description: Fires weekly to clip the best new Kroger digital coupons and send a short recap.
routines.content:
Use the box browser to open the user's Kroger account (kroger.com digital coupons page). If the session is signed out, don't guess credentials: message the user in chat to sign in through the secure sign-in form, and stop until they do. Once in, scroll to load the full list of available digital coupons and rank them by savings (biggest dollar or percent value first). Always clip any categories the user asked to always clip. Also clip the other good ones by savings, skipping low-value filler. Kroger caps clipped coupons at about 248; if the card is full, don't unclip anything without telling the user. Don't buy anything, add to cart, or change settings. Then message the user a short, plain list of what you clipped (item, savings) plus a few other interesting deals you did not clip. No recipes, meal plans, or shopping lists, and don't email anyone. If nothing is worth clipping, stay quiet.
